title: sdk(python/ts/go): unify auth/retries & streaming ergonomics; parity fixes + version bumps
author: Aisha Rahman
description: Motivation: multiple SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) had divergent auth retry semantics and streaming ergonomics which increased maintenance burden and caused subtle behavioral differences in client code. This PR unifies the auth token refresh/retry contract, standardizes streaming iterator APIs, fixes several parity gaps, and bumps SDK package versions. Summary of changes: 1) Auth/retries: unified AuthMiddleware that centralizes token refresh, retry backoff (exp backoff + jitter) and idempotency checks. Token refresh is now non-blocking for streaming reads (see streaming changes). 2) Streaming ergonomics: iterator-based streaming helpers across SDKs; server/control messages separated from payload events; improved cancellation handling and deterministic resource cleanup. 3) Parity fixes: aligned response envelope shapes, consistent error codes, and added missing helper utilities (is_transient_error, retryable_status_codes). 4) Version bumps: python 1.4.0 -> 1.5.0, typescript 0.9.7 -> 0.10.0, go v0.8.3 -> v0.9.0; changelogs updated. 5) Tests & CI: expanded unit/integration coverage for auth refresh and streaming cancellation; added cross-sdk contract tests in redwood-examples harness. Migration notes: existing clients should not see behavior changes for simple sync calls; streaming callers should prefer the new iterator helpers for deterministic cleanup. Callers that relied on implicit blocking token refresh during long-lived streams should migrate to the provided non-blocking refresh callback to avoid transient NotAuthenticated errors during refresh. Checklist: - [x] Implement AuthMiddleware and wire into SDKs - [x] Add streaming iterator helpers and docs snippets - [x] Add compatibility shims for older clients - [x] Update version numbers and changelogs - [x] Add unit/integration tests - [x] Manual smoke on macOS/Linux containers Related: ENG-1421 (unify retries), ENG-1438 (streaming ergonomics).
